name: Pangai
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage names it as the group's base and only town (about 2,500 people), with harbour, shops and churches; arguable as a spot (town stays a spot only when it has its own draws).
objection: Against: one counted source, a service village; its draws (Baker grave, churches, Mystery Cross) are listed separately or fail. For: the main town people walk and cycle around.

name: Lifuka
reason: Rule 3: the island is an area wrapping Pangai, Foa, Poseidon's Gate and the airport; Wikivoyage lists it only as the gateway, no distinct thing to see.
objection: Strongest case for keep: the island is the base visitors cycle around, but its sights are separate entries.

name: Lotofoa Methodist Church
reason: Rule 2 church clause: Wikivoyage singles out a carved coconut-wood ceiling (an interior), but it is one counted source and a short visit.
objection: For: a named interior feature. Against: sole source is one line, no public access or hours info, village church.

name: Pangai Free Wesleyan Church
reason: Rule 2: tourism board lists it under Culture with no interior or feature described; a local parish church seen from the street.
objection: For: a tourism board names it. Against: nothing to see or do stated.

name: Sangata Teleisia o Avila
reason: Rule 2: called 'striking' by the tourism board but no interior, art or tour is described; local church.
objection: For: a tourism board listing. Against: only an adjective, one source, no activity.

name: Mystery Cross
reason: Rule 3: a small spiritual monument in Pangai, a minor memorial-type stop with a ten-minute look.
objection: For: tourism board free-activity listing. Against: minor monument, one source, 0 views.

name: Poseidon's Gate
reason: Rule 1/3: Wikivoyage names the rock terraces on Lifuka's east coast as a stop; second-tier natural feature, one counted source, no detail.
objection: Against: single line source, 0 views, unclear access. For: scenic coastal feature a guide names.

name: Foa Petroglyphs
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage names ancient petroglyphs at Foa's north end; heritage stop, one source, short visit, unclear access.
objection: Against: sparse single-line source. For: genuine archaeological sight a guide lists.

name: Foa Island
reason: Rule 3: an island/area whose only named contents (petroglyphs, wreck) are separate candidates; causeway isle with a lodge.
objection: Strongest keep case: causeway island visitors cycle to, but nothing distinct to do beyond its parts.

name: Port-au-Prince Wreck
reason: Rule 2: a dive site reached only by diving operators, no land stop; the operator experience is not a spot.
objection: For: Wikivoyage names it with a famous history. Against: not a place a visitor generally goes to see.

name: ʻUiha
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage names the island's royal burial grounds with pyramids; cultural site by short boat ride, one source, access and respect limits unclear.
objection: Against: royal burial ground may not welcome visitors, one source. For: distinctive heritage site, 814 views.

name: Kao
reason: Rule 1: two counted tourism-board pages (free activities, land adventures) so source count is solid; the 0 views is a script artefact, since the Wikipedia article is titled Kao (island) and the wiki field 'Kao (volcano)' did not resolve. Rule 2 doubt: small boat only, no path to the summit, so visitors see it from the water.
objection: Against: nothing to do on it, it is a view from a boat and neighbours Tofua. For: Tonga's highest point and a tourism-board-listed draw.

name: Uoleva
reason: Rules 1-3: two counted sources (tourism board free activities, Wikivoyage); secluded beach island with an eco-retreat, a second-tier beach stop.
objection: Against: low-tide walking is dangerous and views are modest; but beach and swimming are a real half-day.

name: Luahoko Island
reason: Rule 1: one Wikivoyage source for a tiny uninhabited white-sand island day trip; a beach stop, but reachable only by chartered boat and thinly sourced.
objection: For: classic desert-island beach stop. Against: one source, 244 views, no facilities.
